scope: E3b: actual checked caller, one static direct BL to the unchanged M1 copy

claims.claim: arbitrary size_t split/n are checked before copying
claims.target: vp2_copy_split: caller 80 bytes, embedded copy 76 bytes; public functional/access contracts
claims.logical_conditions: non-NULL owned ordinary RAM of the supplied capacity L, nowrap and separated from code; separate valid aligned private stack of 16 bytes; initial entry registers and source snapshot
claims.providers: the caller supplies the owned root and stack; CBZ/CMP/unsigned branches establish 0 < split < L, n <= split and n <= L-split; arithmetic and containment theorems derive both subregions and the unchanged M1 copy preconditions
claims.external_trust: the actual region really has L live exclusive bytes; numeric checks alone do not establish physical mappings, lifetime or ownership; OS/allocator maintenance and root-to-memory correspondence remain external
claims.change: dynamic split/n bounds are no longer caller preconditions; they are proved consequences of the actual successful machine path; validity of the supplied capacity still comes from the ownership root

claims.claim: success copies the initial prefix; failure returns 1 with the root unchanged and no data accesses
claims.target: all four rejection paths, successful call/return, conditional writable data frame and access trace
claims.logical_conditions: the same root/stack geometry; no successful-guard assumption in the public contract
claims.providers: actual branch/argument/SP/LR/BL/RET instructions, unchanged M1 functional and strong access theorems, containment and frame rules
claims.external_trust: architectural events are not a complete observation of caches/speculation/power; exact mapped code and the ISA/CPU relation remain assumptions
claims.change: the failure path does not form the subregion, decrement SP, access data or call copy; successful stack and data effects are separated

claims.claim: actual machine success justifies E3a permission transitions for the same sizes
claims.target: ve_split_protocol_contract: actual postcondition plus status-zero implies the borrow/use/return protocol
claims.logical_conditions: one current sequential ghost ledger; root owner/epoch binds to the arena and its capacity; no invalidation or competing update during the operation
claims.providers: the machine return-status theorem implies the checked guard; E3a borrow, permission and return theorems construct the protocol for exactly val L, val split and val n
claims.external_trust: physical ownership correspondence and current-ledger discipline are not enforced by a general borrow checker in this prototype; HOL facts remain classical, not linear resources
claims.change: entry conditions are now connected to actual branch results and the actual BL code; ghost ownership values add no runtime code or storage

claims.claim: malformed checks and argument construction have concrete violations
claims.target: five separately linked mutations: split range, input/output length, wrong subtraction, overlapping target
claims.logical_conditions: explicit loaded states satisfy the original public root/stack precondition; no guard is smuggled into that precondition; all extra numeric disjointness/alignment facts are proved closed
claims.providers: finite ARM executions and concrete initial-state witnesses; native normal controls, wrong-status/data observations and protected-page faults
claims.external_trust: native test harness and host CPU/OS; finite witnesses do not by themselves negate every general Hoare proposition
claims.change: a bad caller can violate the copy's preconditions even when the copy itself is proved; raw finite execution, not the inapplicable child theorem, supplies those counterexamples

current_software_boundaries: current-ledger enforcement is not implemented as a language checker
interpretation: These current software boundaries can be reduced by further verification. They are not identified with mathematically unavoidable physical limits.
not_claimed: unconditional memory safety for a caller that lies about L
universal fastest code or physical real-time bound
